programme: A G1/S checkpoint-control network built around the MYC–MAX axis and its brakes: MXI1 antagonises MYC/MAX at shared target promoters (MYC, MYCN, CCNB1, ODC1); TFDP2 partners E2F to drive S-phase genes (PCNA, RFC3, MYC); JARID2 (a PRC2 accessory factor) represses the CCND1/CDK4/RB1/NOTCH1 module; ZNF304 silences the CDKN2A/CDKN2B locus; SALL2 and KLF7 converge on the CDKN1A/CDKN1B (p21/p27) brake. ELK4 and ETV3 sit upstream as MAPK-responsive ETS-family factors (EGR1, FOS, KRAS, MYC, DUSP6) that feed proliferative signal into this same MYC/cyclin circuitry. Together these are the restriction-point machinery that decides whether a cell divides.
role_in_a: No documented role. Open Targets records no Fibromyalgia association for any of these factors (ZNF410, not a carrying factor, has a weak 0.295 percentile). If this checkpoint set is genuinely concordant across FM patient-group blood networks, the more defensible reading is that it tracks differences in circulating lymphocyte/myeloid proliferative activity between subgroups, not an FM-specific pathogenic process — that reading is inference, not something retrieved.
role_in_b: Established. Loss of RB–E2F/CDKN2A/CDKN1A checkpoint control and MYC/MAX dysregulation are hallmark drivers of NSCLC/LUSC proliferation, consistent with the elevated Open Targets percentiles for MXI1 (0.9662), KLF7 (0.5898), JARID2 (0.5313) and SALL2 (0.5568). Two factors are directly documented: ELK4 promotes NSCLC progression (PMID 39969091, 35526007) and KLF7 activates CDK1 via PPP1R14C to drive lung squamous cell carcinoma (PMID 41699008).
shared_axis: No publication ties this checkpoint module to fibromyalgia. The only plausible bridge is that the same generic cell-cycle/checkpoint wiring is reused whenever proliferative state differs across patient subgroups — tracking immune-cell cycling in FM blood and tumor-cell cycling in lung tissue — but this is a structural analogy, not a documented shared mechanism.
reasoning: The programme is coherent and its lung-cancer role is independently anchored by Open Targets percentiles and two direct papers (ELK4, KLF7), so this is not incoherent. But every factor's Fibromyalgia record is empty or negligible, and the FM–lung link therefore rests entirely on reasoning about shared cell-cycle wiring rather than on anything retrieved, which is why this lands as unexpected/moderate rather than supported or established.
support: PMID 39969091 — ELK4 transcriptionally promotes MSI2-mediated NSCLC progression via TGF-β signalling. PMID 35526007 — a tRNA-derived fragment drives NSCLC malignancy through an ELK4-linked HSPB1/MED29 axis. PMID 41699008 — KLF7 transcriptionally activates PPP1R14C to unleash CDK1 activity and drive lung squamous cell carcinoma. No PMID retrieved supports any factor specifically in fibromyalgia.
how_to_falsify: In fibromyalgia PBMC RNA-seq, test whether expression/activity of the checkpoint targets (CCNB1, CDKN2A/B, CDKN1A, PCNA, RFC3, CCND1) tracks lymphocyte Ki67/proliferation markers rather than FM clinical subgroup or pain severity; if it tracks blood-cell-cycle state only, the concordance is a cell-composition artifact, not a shared disease programme. Separately, ChIP/CUT&RUN for ZNF304 and JARID2 at CDKN2A and CCND1 in FM PBMCs versus lung tumor cells — the ReMap record already shows near-absent binding for MXI1 (0/7 targets) and JARID2 (0/7 targets) in the existing catalogue, so if binding cannot be demonstrated in either tissue, the module's transcriptional logic is unsupported.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (FM) versus lung (cancer), so a shared transcriptional module more plausibly reflects convergent circuitry (immune-cell cycling vs. tumor-cell cycling) than a common pathogenic axis. There is only 1 independent cohort pair behind the 112 patient-group comparisons, so this is unreplicated across cohorts, only across within-cohort subgroup splits. Support ranges from 72/112 (MXI1) down to 48/112 (ETV3) — none near saturation. ReMap binding evidence for the module's core repressors is sparse (MXI1 0/7, JARID2 0/7 targets bound). The tissue-generic exclusion list removed BCL6, RELB, FOXO1, FOXO4, BCL3, EBF1 and NR3C2 — the inflammatory/immune master regulators one might otherwise reach for to explain an FM–cancer link — so that route is specifically foreclosed by the data, not an oversight. Single-view exclusions (GATA2, BATF, NFATC3, HEY1) likewise show plausible immune/differentiation factors did not generalize past one subgroup, reinforcing that what actually recurs here is the cell-cycle/checkpoint set, not a broader immune signature.
